title: Per-layer hybrid INT8/FP8 KV quant profiles: calibration protocol and latency-quality A/B evaluation
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Design, implement, and validate a per-layer hybrid quantization profile for the KV cache that mixes INT8 and FP8 formats to reduce tail latency while keeping generation quality within an acceptable degradation budget. We will define a calibration protocol that produces stable per-layer scale factors, an automated profile selection policy that chooses INT8 vs FP8 per-layer based on expected sequence length and cache size, and an evaluation harness that measures p50/p95/p99 latency and a small suite of automated and human quality checks. This ticket covers design, calibration pipeline, experiments, and rollout gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration pipeline produces deterministic per-layer scales with <2% variance across 3 independent runs. 2) Hybrid profiles reduce p99 token latency by >=15% for typical chat workloads compared to full-FP16 baseline without batching changes. 3) Quality regressions: automated metrics (perplexity on validation prompts) increase <=1.5% and human-rated coherence/accuracy drop <=2 points on a 100-point rubric. 4) Profiles are checkpointed, annotated, and can be enabled via runtime config flag with safe fallback to full-FP16 or full-FP8.
testing_plan:
- Calibration: run 3 independent calibration passes on two representative corpora (instruction-dialogue, long-context docs).
- Offline eval: measure perplexity, answer-exactness on a 1k prompt holdout, and token-level logprob shifts per layer.
- Human eval: 200 pairs of model outputs (hybrid vs FP16) rated for correctness and fluency by 3 raters.
- Perf: synthetic and production-like load tests to capture p50/p95/p99 for token generation across sequence lengths 64/512/2048.
- Safety: smoke checks for numerical instabilities and NaN propagation in KV retrieval code.
benchmarks_summary: Preliminary runs (Mar 07): model=open-llm-13B-chat, hardware=A100-40GB, baseline FP16 p99 token latency=210ms at seq=512. Hybrid per-layer INT8/FP8 profile reduced p99 to 168ms (-20%), p95 from 102ms to 86ms (-16%), p50 from 34ms to 30ms (-12%). Automated perplexity increased 0.8% on the validation suite. Human rating pilot (n=60) showed average quality delta -0.9 points on 100-point rubric. These are early and noisy; full calibration + more seeds required.
design_decisions: Use per-layer asymmetric INT8 for attention matmul weights where dynamic range is narrow and switch to FP8 for projection layers with high dynamic range.
Store explicit per-layer scale + zero-point metadata in profile artifact to enable deterministic round-trip and offline verification.
Calibration will use a stratified sampling of context lengths and token distributions; use median-of-means for scale estimation to improve robustness.
Profile selection policy: offline scoring that predicts expected MSE vs FP16 given seq length and cached KV footprint, then materialize runtime rule-set mapping seq-length ranges to profile variants.
Fail-open behavior: if any layer has unstable calibration (NaN or >10% run-to-run variance) or runtime detects numerical errors, fall back to FP16 for that request and emit telemetry.
Keep quantized KV on GPU memory to avoid copy overheads; add lightweight checksum to detect corruption after serialization.
Expose feature as an opt-in flag behind rollout gate and per-customer allowlist for Dedicated/Private customers until validated.
Do not change compilation kernels for this iteration; reuse existing INT8/FP8 execution paths to reduce risk and speed iteration.
